effort: Keep the body organized while switching between running, shuffling and backpedaling on a known route.
brief: E2 follows a short box with three gait corners. A backward W prepares diagonal backward force, a crossing route challenges obtuse plants, a crossover reversal changes lateral gait direction, and two small single-leg landing tasks isolate backward and rotational acceptance.
marker: In E2, record control at each of the three corners and whether the athlete maintains the declared facing through the run–shuffle–backpedal–shuffle sequence; a completed route with crossed feet is not automatically a valid attempt.
readiness: Verify backward and same-leg rotational landing competence independently during the scheduled small attempts. Keep route pace controlled; the second/third corner must not become a fatigue test.
space: Use a measured 9 m × 6 m bay including each final stopping continuation. Mark route order and direction clearly before each attempt. No partner calls, moving targets or overlapping courses are used. The full bay width is still a delivery requirement, not confirmed inventory.

drills.name: W Drill Backpedal Cuts — short route
drills.execution: Face forward throughout and backpedal through three 1 m alternating rear-diagonal legs, then stop over 1.5 m. Keep feet low and do not spin to run.
drills.job: Prepare backward pushes toward alternating diagonals while preserving facing.
drills.layout: Mark three short rear-diagonal legs and clear the final 1.5 m backward stopping continuation; the route contains both left and right changes.
drills.difference: Backward gait through linked changes; Class 9's W used forward running.
drills.regress: Reduce speed/step length if the athlete crosses heels or falls behind the base.

drills.name: Box Drill — Sprint, Shuffle, Backpedal
drills.execution: Use a 1.5 m square: run forward, shuffle sideways, backpedal, then shuffle back to the starting corner; stop over 1.5 m on the last heading. Chest keeps its initial facing.
drills.job: Main planned gait switching while keeping a useful base at each corner.
drills.layout: 6 m route travel plus 1.5 m final stop. The three intermediate corners are cuts; the start/finish is a terminal stop. Clear the final extension outside the square.
drills.difference: Four sides with three distinct gait transitions, unlike the triangle's two corners or a single transition.
drills.regress: Lower course pace if the athlete changes facing or crosses feet to recover.
drills.exposure: 3 cuts and 4 braking episodes per route.

drills.name: X Crossing Route — two obtuse plants
drills.execution: On a 1.5 m square, run lower-left to upper-right, across to upper-left, then diagonally to lower-right; stop over 2 m on that diagonal. Mirror the route for the other side.
drills.job: Prepare obtuse plants while the next exit crosses the earlier travel line.
drills.layout: Legs are about 2.12, 1.5 and 2.12 m, total 5.74 m. One athlete owns the crossing and final 2 m stop; no cone touch or extra return.
drills.difference: Crossing diagonals linked by a transverse leg create two obtuse plants; neither the W nor Z has this crossing topology.
drills.regress: Reduce entry speed at both far corners if the athlete loops around instead of controlling the plant.
drills.exposure: 2 cuts and 3 braking episodes per route.

drills.name: Crossover Run Reversal
drills.execution: Crossover-run 2 m along the lane, brake before the cone and return 2 m with crossover running in the opposite direction; stop over 2 m.
drills.job: Redirect a crossing gait without the feet tangling at the turn.
drills.layout: Start at 4, turn at 6, return to 4 and stop by 2; mirror 6 → 4 → 6 → 8. Keep the chest obliquely oriented rather than using a forward sprint turn.
drills.difference: Crossing lateral gait enters and leaves the reversal; earlier lateral reversals used non-crossing shuffle contacts.
drills.regress: Lower entry speed if the athlete needs an uncontrolled spin or extra hop.

drills.name: Single-Leg Backward Hop to Stick
drills.execution: Hop backward a very short distance, no more than 0.2 m, landing on the same leg for a 2 s hold.
drills.job: Own backward force acceptance when a single leg remains the support.
drills.layout: Inspect the empty landing space before starting; use the middle of the lane with clear fall margins.
drills.difference: Backward same-leg landing instead of the earlier bilateral backward jump or forward/diagonal same-leg hop.
drills.regress: Make the hop nearly in place if the pelvis falls behind the heel; stop if single-leg control remains absent.

drills.name: Quarter-Turn Single-Leg Hop to Stick
drills.execution: Make a very low hop, rotate up to 90 degrees away from the free leg and land on the same leg; hold 2 s. No travel target.
drills.job: Coordinate the pelvis and support foot before receiving rotational force.
drills.layout: 3 m × 3 m clear landing area; no approach or rebound. Record actual turn angle.
drills.difference: Same-leg landing during the airborne turn, rather than the bilateral quarter-turn or opposite-leg rotational bound.
drills.regress: Reduce rotation and height if the foot and knee land misaligned; do not force 90 degrees.
drills.exposure: 1 unilateral landing per leg; body rotation is not a running cut.

light.job: Maintain pelvis-over-foot control when facing and travel direction differ.
Support foot-edge control at crossing-gait and backward corners.

strength.job: Load a controlled backward step and forward return relevant to the gait changes.
Maintain hip-extension force for running exits after backward travel.
Maintain frontal-plane force for the box's lateral legs.
Maintain knee-flexor braking support without extra dynamic volume.
Maintain adductor support across the lateral corners.
Maintain bent-knee ankle force for low gait transitions.

previous_review: Class 9 prescribed ten discrete cuts, four unilateral landings and eight primary bouts. No actual second-corner quality or recovery has been reported.
progression: Apply a known multi-gait route with short 1–1.5 m entry legs. The added corner count is balanced by one W route, two box routes and low support doses; no speed increase is prescribed. If actual linked-corner control is not established, lower pace and record incomplete work where necessary.
strength_progression: Keep all lifts at one working round and target reserve unchanged. Reuse the Class 6 reverse lunge/hip thrust rather than introducing a new heavy lift while gait complexity changes; soleus replaces straight-knee calf emphasis for the lowered transition posture.
audit: Counted three box corners, not four, and two X-route corners, not each centre crossing. The two unilateral landing drills have different force directions and remain one small attempt per leg. Whole routes stop after the prescribed traversal.
next: Next class reduces route density for high-quality reorganization and deceptive entries; review actual corner quality and fatigue before final application.

light_entries.name: Hip Airplane — supported
light_entries.execution: Bodyweight, hand support and slight hip hinge. Slowly open/close pelvis through a small owned arc without rolling the stance foot.
light_entries.rest: Keep easy; rest 30 s between legs.
light_entries.regress: Reduce arc or use more hand support if knee/foot rotates uncontrollably.
light_entries.job: Maintain pelvis-over-foot control when facing and travel direction differ.

light_entries.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion — self-anchored (proposed)
light_entries.execution: Sit securely, use the other foot to hold a light loop; turn the working forefoot slightly outward against tension, 2 s return, keep knee still.
light_entries.regress: Use less tension/range for toe gripping or whole-leg rotation.
light_entries.source: Proposed exact setup; no verified identifier
light_entries.alternative: Use instead of the band, gentle hand resistance at the outer forefoot with the same easy reps if a loop cannot be secured.
light_entries.job: Support foot-edge control at crossing-gait and backward corners.

strength_entries.name: Reverse Lunge — two dumbbells
strength_entries.execution: Step backward under control, lower 2 s and drive through the original front foot to return. Keep knee tracking with the foot.
strength_entries.rest: Rest 60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce step length/load for an uncontrolled backward reach or front-heel lift.
strength_entries.job: Load a controlled backward step and forward return relevant to the gait changes.

strength_entries.name: Hip Thrust — dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: Upper back on a stable bench, dumbbell secured over pelvis; rise to hip extension without arching the back, lower 2 s.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce load/range for lumbar extension or hamstring cramp.
strength_entries.alternative: If bench geometry is unsuitable, use instead a loaded dynamic floor glute bridge at the same rep/effort and preparation dose.
strength_entries.job: Maintain hip-extension force for running exits after backward travel.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Maintain frontal-plane force for the box's lateral legs.

strength_entries.name: Glute Bridge Iso Hold — long-lever hamstring variant
strength_entries.execution: bilateral. Heels farther from the hips than a standard bridge, knees still bent; bodyweight or a securely hand-held sandbag over the pelvis to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Try to pull the heels toward the body without sliding them; keep ribs down. Bring heels closer or remove load for cramp/lost height; stop for symptoms.
strength_entries.job: Maintain knee-flexor braking support without extra dynamic volume.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Maintain adductor support across the lateral corners.

strength_entries.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
strength_entries.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.
strength_entries.job: Maintain bent-knee ankle force for low gait transitions.
